newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Stad R'dam sees 12-20 pct profit growth.
newsitem.headline: Stad R'dam sees 12-20 pct profit growth.

text.p: Insurance firm Stad Rotterdam Anno 1720 NV, to be renamed ASR Verzekeringsgroep, said on Thursday it expected a 12 to 20 percent growth in net earnings in 1997 compared to 1996.
Stad Rotterdam chairman Carlo de Swart told Reuters in a telephone interview ahead of the new listing tomorrow that earnings per share were expected to increase between 12 to 20 percent.
"Earnings are expected to increase 12 to 20 percent and earnings per share are expected to rise somewhere in between those figure as well," he said.
The medium sized Dutch insurer had net profits of 156.9 million guilders in 1996.
ASR Verzekeringsgroep is a combination of Stad Rotterdam and unlisted insurer De Amersfoortse.
In April Stad Rotterdam said it was planning to buy the remaining stake in unlisted De Amersfoortse, in which it already held 55 percent.
Last month Stad Rotterdam said its shareholders had approved the formation of a new holding company. The move followed Stad Rotterdam's merger with De Amersfoortse.
The merger with De Amersfoortse was taking effect from April 1, 1997, De Swart said.
Stad Rotterdam shares closed at 92.00 guilders on Thursday, a rise of one guilder compared to the previous trading day.
De Swart said the firm was not mulling a share split to attract more investors now that the stock was moving towards the 100-guilder level.
"There are no concrete plans for a share split," De Swart said.
Muenchener Rueckversicherung holds a stake of some 11 percent in ASR Verzekeringsgroep. Other big shareholders are Fortis Amev with 20 percent, ING with 20 percent and unlisted insurer Achmea.

De Swart said he expected growth in turnover from life insurance products with a regular premium instalment of some 13 to 15 percent annually and added it was more difficult to forecast growth for single premium life policies.
De Swart said an annual growth of four to six percent in turnover for the non-life sector, excluding health care, would be "normal" for the coming years.
Stad Rotterdam had a turnover of 4.5 billion guilders in 1996 of which De Amersfoortse contributed 1.16 billion guilders.
Premium income for Stad Rotterdam's life insurance was 1.58 billion guilders in 1996 and non-life was 1.62 billion.

ASR verzekeringsgroep is the new name of the listed company which holds 100 percent of the shares of two subsidiaries -- Stad Rotterdam and De Amersfoortse verzekeringen. ASR also has a 70 percent shareholding in Europeesche Verzekering Maatschappij.
"Each of the companies will retain its own brand name," it said.
